key_insight: A world model can look realistic without simulating events correctly. This paper separates prediction type from generation strategy to investigate how each shapes learned dynamics; the provided abstract does not report the final comparative results.
problem_solved: Visual quality alone cannot establish whether a world model behaves faithfully. Common approaches also bundle categorical or continuous prediction with different generation strategies, making their individual effects difficult to assess.
method: Systematically compare categorical and continuous prediction under both next-token and iterative whole-frame generation.
Use controlled 2D and 3D environments to study learned dynamics.
Evaluate dynamics validity, calibration, and visual quality as distinct criteria.
impact: For practitioners, the study emphasizes evaluating behavioral correctness and calibration alongside visual realism. Its controlled comparisons are designed to clarify which modeling choices influence reliable simulation.
visual_elements: A 2×2 comparison grid: categorical versus continuous prediction, crossed with next-token versus iterative whole-frame generation.
Paired scene sequences illustrating the difference between visually convincing motion and valid dynamics.
A three-axis evaluation graphic labeled dynamics validity, calibration, and visual quality, without invented scores.
Simple 2D and 3D environment icons representing the controlled test settings.
paper_title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models
paper_authors: Sarah Parisot, Melanie Fernandez Pradier, David Bignell, Sergio Valcarcel Macua, Katja Hofmann
